mission: Continue foreign canonical thinning around major patristic author clusters while preserving Work identity across languages, editions, volumes and source corpora.

clusters.author: Basil of Caesarea
clusters.rule: collections/volumes are containers; canonicalize identifiable works beneath them

clusters.author: Gregory of Nazianzus
clusters.rule: do not collapse the entire author corpus into one Work; preserve individual orations/letter groups where stable work identity exists

clusters.author: Gregory of Nyssa
clusters.rule: merge translations/editions/witnesses under each work; modern critical editions remain edition-level and rights-specific

clusters.author: John Cassian
clusters.rule: Books/Conferences are structural children of the canonical work unless source evidence identifies separately circulated works

clusters.author: Jerome
clusters.hardExclusion: Jerome Bible translations and Scripture text do not enter Dawn translation product; non-Scripture writings remain eligible

clusters.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
clusters.rule: Ecclesiastical History is one canonical Work with books as internal structure, not ten books in holdings count

authorityAndRights.principle: Work identity is source-independent; readable witnesses and rights remain source/edition-specific.
authorityAndRights.publicDomainHistoricalEnglish: NPNF Series II historical volumes provide strong edition/witness anchors for Eusebius, Gregory of Nyssa, Jerome, Gregory Nazianzen, Basil and Cassian.
authorityAndRights.modernCriticalTexts: May improve identity/alignment but are never presumed reusable; retain file/edition license gates.
authorityAndRights.dubiaSpuria: Keep disputed/spurious attribution as explicit authority state and never silently merge into an author's secure corpus.

readerProjection.frontEnd: one Work -> available original witnesses -> eligible historical translation witnesses -> generated zh-Hant reading projection
readerProjection.rule: Chinese translation never becomes a duplicate Work or fake published Chinese edition.

classificationConsequence: Patristics remains a period/tradition facet across the reader-facing families, not a separate isolated library. A single Work can carry multiple browse families.
next: Continue from author clusters into concrete Work-level admission records, prioritizing works with stable identity + readable public-domain witness + cover/title-page source, then deduplicate against PRDL/Open Christian Data/CatholicCorpus.
